index 38da1e6..e8f6f43 100644
--- a/django/db/migrations/serializer.py
+++ b/django/db/migrations/serializer.py
@@ -125,6 +125,30 @@ class EnumSerializer(BaseSerializer):
     def serialize(self):
         enum_class = self.value.__class__
         module = enum_class.__module__
+        
+        # Check if the enum value's name is a valid member name
+        if self.value.name in enum_class.__members__:
+            # Simple case: the value is a single enum member
+            return (
+                "%s.%s[%r]" % (module, enum_class.__qualname__, self.value.name),
+                {"import %s" % module},
+            )
+        
+        # Complex case: the value is a combination of flags (e.g., re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE)
+        # In this case, self.value.name will be something like "IGNORECASE|UNICODE"
+        # We need to decompose it and reconstruct it using OR operations
+        if "|" in self.value.name:
+            # Split the name and reconstruct using OR operations
+            names = self.value.name.split("|")
+            parts = []
+            for name in names:
+                parts.append("%s.%s[%r]" % (module, enum_class.__qualname__, name))
+            return (
+                " | ".join(parts),
+                {"import %s" % module},
+            )
+        
+        # Fallback: use the name as-is (this may fail at runtime, but it's better than nothing)
         return (
             "%s.%s[%r]" % (module, enum_class.__qualname__, self.value.name),
             {"import %s" % module},

+#!/usr/bin/env python
+import re
+import enum
+from django.db.migrations.writer import MigrationWriter
+
+# Test 1: Single flag
+print("Test 1: Single flag")
+result = MigrationWriter.serialize(re.UNICODE)
+print(f"  Serialized: {result}")
+
+# Test 2: Combined flags
+print("\nTest 2: Combined flags")
+combined = re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE
+result = MigrationWriter.serialize(combined)
+print(f"  Serialized: {result}")
+
+# Test 3: Round-trip test
+print("\nTest 3: Round-trip test")
+combined = re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE
+string, imports = MigrationWriter.serialize(combined)
+print(f"  Serialized: {string}")
+print(f"  Imports: {imports}")
+
+# Execute the serialized code
+d = {}
+exec("\n".join(imports) + "\ntest_value_result = " + string, globals(), d)
+result = d["test_value_result"]
+print(f"  Result: {result}")
+print(f"  Expected: {combined}")
+print(f"  Match: {result == combined}")
+
+# Test 4: Test with IntFlagEnum
+print("\nTest 4: Test with IntFlagEnum")
+
+class IntFlagEnum(enum.IntFlag):
+    A = 1
+    B = 2
+
+combined = IntFlagEnum.A | IntFlagEnum.B
+result = MigrationWriter.serialize(combined)
+print(f"  Serialized: {result}")
+
+# Round-trip test
+string, imports = result
+d = {}
+exec("\n".join(imports) + "\ntest_value_result = " + string, globals(), d)
+result = d["test_value_result"]
+print(f"  Result: {result}")
+print(f"  Expected: {combined}")
+print(f"  Match: {result == combined}")

+#!/usr/bin/env python
+import re
+import enum
+
+# Test 1: Single flag
+print("Test 1: Single flag")
+print(f"  re.UNICODE: {re.UNICODE}")
+print(f"  Type: {type(re.UNICODE)}")
+print(f"  Has name: {hasattr(re.UNICODE, 'name')}")
+if hasattr(re.UNICODE, 'name'):
+    print(f"  Name: {re.UNICODE.name}")
+
+# Test 2: Combined flags
+print("\nTest 2: Combined flags")
+combined = re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE
+print(f"  re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE: {combined}")
+print(f"  Type: {type(combined)}")
+print(f"  Has name: {hasattr(combined, 'name')}")
+if hasattr(combined, 'name'):
+    print(f"  Name: {combined.name}")
+else:
+    print(f"  Name: None (this is the problem!)")
+
+# Test 3: Check enum._decompose
+print("\nTest 3: Check enum._decompose")
+if hasattr(enum, '_decompose'):
+    decomposed = enum._decompose(type(combined), combined)
+    print(f"  Decomposed: {decomposed}")
+    print(f"  Type of decomposed: {type(decomposed)}")
+else:
+    print("  enum._decompose not available")
+
+# Test 4: Check if we can reconstruct the value
+print("\nTest 4: Reconstruct value")
+enum_class = type(combined)
+print(f"  Enum class: {enum_class}")
+print(f"  Enum class module: {enum_class.__module__}")
+print(f"  Enum class qualname: {enum_class.__qualname__}")
+
+# Try to decompose
+if hasattr(enum, '_decompose'):
+    decomposed = enum._decompose(enum_class, combined)
+    print(f"  Decomposed: {decomposed}")
+    
+    # Try to reconstruct
+    if decomposed:
+        names = [m.name for m in decomposed]
+        print(f"  Names: {names}")
+        
+        # Try to reconstruct using OR
+        reconstructed = enum_class[names[0]]
+        for name in names[1:]:
+            reconstructed = reconstructed | enum_class[name]
+        print(f"  Reconstructed: {reconstructed}")
+        print(f"  Reconstructed == original: {reconstructed == combined}")

+#!/usr/bin/env python
+import re
+import enum
+
+# Test decomposing the combined flag
+combined = re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE
+print(f"Combined value: {combined}")
+print(f"Combined name: {combined.name}")
+
+# Try to decompose manually
+print(f"\nManual decomposition:")
+enum_class = re.RegexFlag
+members = []
+for member in enum_class:
+    if member.value != 0 and (combined.value & member.value) == member.value:
+        # Check if this is a "pure" member (not a combination)
+        # by checking if it's in the original members list
+        if member.name in enum_class.__members__:
+            members.append(member)
+            print(f"  Found: {member.name} = {member.value}")
+
+print(f"\nMembers found: {members}")
+
+# Try to reconstruct
+if members:
+    reconstructed = members[0]
+    for member in members[1:]:
+        reconstructed = reconstructed | member
+    print(f"Reconstructed: {reconstructed}")
+    print(f"Reconstructed == original: {reconstructed == combined}")
+
+# Try a different approach - use the name to decompose
+print(f"\nUsing name decomposition:")
+names = combined.name.split('|')
+print(f"Names: {names}")
+
+# Reconstruct using names
+reconstructed = enum_class[names[0]]
+for name in names[1:]:
+    reconstructed = reconstructed | enum_class[name]
+print(f"Reconstructed: {reconstructed}")
+print(f"Reconstructed == original: {reconstructed == combined}")
